items.title: Game of Thrones Star Kit Harington Isn't a Gamer, But He's Excited for Grand Theft Auto 6
items.description: Game of Thrones star Kit Harington has confessed that he isn't much of a gamer, but wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Game of Thrones star Kit Harington has confessed that he isn't much of a gamer, but wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6.

The actor best known for playing Jon Snow reflected on his experience with the gaming world with Josh Horowitz in a recent interview. After recalling his experience working on Silent Hill: Revelation, a live-action film based on the beloved horror gaming franchise, he was asked if he was much of a gamer. Harington noted he didn't have much experience with the Silent Hill games, but played a bit of Tekken, Mario Kart, Diddy Kong Racing, and most recently, Hogwarts Legacy.

When Horowitz asked if he'd ever dabbled in Grand Theft Auto, Harington said that he wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6 after seeing some of the advertising. He went on to express an admiration for videos that mimic GTA's tropes in real life. All of this sort of goes to show that the GTA 6 effect is beginning to happen, as even non-gamers are getting pulled in by its trance.

Rockstar is spending a boatload of cash to get the game in front of as many people as possible. It has assembled an Avengers-level ensemble of musicians to craft an original soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto 6, spent nearly $1 million on a "Welcome to Vice City" sign in Miami, and is likely only going to continue to ramp things up as we get closer to launch. NBA star Steven Adams also joked that he expects the performance of the league to drop when GTA 6 releases in November.

As for Harington specifically, he didn't say whether or not he will actually end up playing GTA 6 or not. He's had some experience in the gaming world, as he was the main antagonist in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and voiced Jon Snow in Telltale's Game of Thrones video game. His next big role will be playing Gildroy Lockhart in HBO's Harry Potter TV series, which may explain why he recently dabbled in Hogwarts Legacy.

Photo by Kristina Bumphrey/Variety via Getty Images

items.title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls PC Sales Figures and Player Count Spark Worry From Players About Game's Longevity
items.description: It’s been over a month since Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls released, and its early sales figures and player counts on PC are sparking concern within the fighting game community about its longevity.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
It’s been over a month since Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls released, and its early sales figures and player counts on PC are sparking concern within the fighting game community about its longevity.

Arc System Works’ latest tag fighting game has suffered no end of discourse within the FGC; some players love it, while others are severely dissatisfied with its tag system and online matchmaking, and it’s almost impossible to avoid this debate if you’re on fighting game Twitter right now. Most everyone was excited for a new, fast-paced Marvel fighting game from the developers of the highly-lauded Guilty Gear series and Dragon Ball FighterZ — but after launch, that excitement seems to have dwindled into a spiral of frustration.

Data from Steam Charts shows that the title boasts a current active PC player count of 427 players on Steam, with a 24-hour peak of 791 players. The game’s all-time peak on Steam is listed at 13,787 players, but keep in mind that these are just Steam figures and don’t account for PlayStation users.

Sales figures for Tokon on PC have also driven discourse around the game; data from Alinea Analytics shows a cavernous disparity between platforms, with 82% of copies being sold on PlayStation compared to just 18% on Steam. That being said, it has generated an estimated $49.7 million in revenue, selling approximately 750,000 copies across both platforms combined.

Those numbers aren’t anything to sniff at, and it’s worth noting that the competition is stiff. Street Fighter 6 is definitely the most successful fighting game on the market right now, and Tokon was unlikely to ever topple it. The game is certainly seeing success on PlayStation — but its extremely rough launch on PC is likely to blame for the severe disparity between who's playing on what platform.

The game infamously suffered issues with its PC port at launch, to the point where prominent community figure Maximilian Dood literally uninstalled it during one of his live streams in a damning moment that went viral. While a patch was quickly released to help solve these problems, Tokon’s producer admitted that it would be difficult to regain players’ trust after this, and the game’s director, Kazuto Sekine, apologized for the ordeal in an honest statement a month later.

While Tokon appears to be thriving on PlayStation, its comparatively lackluster playerbase on PC and strikingly smaller sales figures on Steam have sparked a debate within the fighting game community as to whether or not the game has what it takes to weather the storm in an increasingly crowded market of IP-based tag fighting games (hello, Invincible VS and Avatar Legends). We also can’t discount the fact that the game was initially blocked in 132 countries due to PSN requirements.

One of the loudest voices in this conversation is Guilty Gear and Smash Bros pro William ‘Leffen’ Hjelte. “Unless Tokon turns the game around gameplay wise by next patch, I'm gonna drop it,” he wrote in a viral post on X/Twitter. “Gameplay aside, I can't even get matches in EU, it feels like the serious playerbase is maybe, at best, 1/10th of Strive’s and 2XKO’s here.

“I genuinely think the game is saveable if they act fast and correctly, but with us not even knowing when the patch is coming and only four characters coming (no date), I think it's probably over, at least if you care about having a big scene. Very sad, I had a lot of high hopes for Tokon.”

I genuinely think the game is saveable if they act fast and correctly but with us not even knowing when the patch is coming and only 4 chars coming (no date) I think its probably over, at least if you care about having a big scene.
Very sad, I had a lot of high hopes for Tokon.

— Leffen (@TSM_Leffen) September 22, 2026

“Dragon Ball FighterZ sold over two million copies in its first week,” another player pointed out. “Tokon probably won't even break one million in six months. This is truly sad that they fumbled such an easy win.”

“Yeah... This game will only have a year's worth of content, and only because it's already made or in the planning stages. I don't think Cyclops will bring in the crowd Tokon needs,” another speculated.

Others, however, are arguing that it’s only been just under two months since the game came out, and are pointing to its success on PlayStation as to why things might not be as grim as some voices in the FGC believe.

“Marvel Tokon came out August 6. Not even two months ago,” YouTuber and prominent community member Mightykeef said. “Not… even… two months ago. I’ve seen such an insane amount of doom posting for a fighting game that has not even been able to breath for two months, lol.”

“Tokon is an incredible fighting game, but it's still a fighting game. Always a niche genre. Hell, one of the goats of the genre, UMVC3, didn't crack 600k in two months,” another pointed out.

“It took Marvel vs Capcom 2 years to become the mythical legend it is. Started in arcade, then ported over to Dreamcast, PS2, Xbox. It’s not gonna happen overnight. And I love Tokon, I want more of it. We need to really end the stupid seasonal DLC crap. Just launch with more characters,” another said.

The FGC culture is so different than I remember. Marvel Tokon came out August 6th. Not even two months ago.

Not… even… two months ago. I’ve seen such an insane amount of doom posting for a fighting game that has not even been able to breath for two months lol https://t.co/1LGW70FoEG

— Mightykeef (@MightyKeef) September 23, 2026

What’s your take on this conversation? Do you think Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is in a healthy state with a bright future ahead, or do you believe that the game is already on its way to irrelevance? Let us know in the comments below.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Shirts Given Away for Free at Tokyo Game Show Are Being Resold Online for Hundreds of Dollars
items.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 shirts that were given away for free exclusively at Tokyo Game Show 2026 are already being resold online for hundreds of dollars.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 shirts that were given away for free exclusively at Tokyo Game Show 2026 are already being resold online for hundreds of dollars.

Attendees at Tokyo Game Show who got the chance to participate in a special immersive screening for GTA 6’s viral Netflix special were treated to commemorative T-shirts to celebrate the occasion.

This screening was the exact same extended trailer that launched on Netflix last month, but with more bells and whistles; it featured tricks like surround sound and 4D haptic effects that correlated with what was happening on screen, letting viewers feel like they were actually tagging along with Jason and Lucia as they fled from the fuzz and held up corner stores.

The experience was so popular that the GTA 6 booth closed after just 10 minutes, having already reached capacity — but savvy fans saw an opportunity to capitalize on the overwhelming demand and make some quick cash.

As spotted by Dexerto, the commemorative T-shirts handed out by PlayStation at the game's TGS 2026 booth for free have already made their way online and are being resold on platforms like eBay for hundreds of dollars.

A quick browse on eBay shows a handful of listings pricing the shirts around $140 - $200, while other goodies that were given out at Rockstar’s booth, like GTA 6-branded stickers and carabiners, are being marked up to the tune of $30 - $40.

This isn’t a new phenomenon, by far; exclusive merchandise like this has become a target for scalpers across several big franchises over the last few years. One Piece’s viral collaboration with Popeye’s is a prime example of this, as scalpers waited in lines that trailed blocks away from their local fast food franchises to snag special Luffy-themed bento boxes, only to list them online for staggeringly high prices.

The same can be said of the Pokemon Trading Card scene; scalpers have become ravenous for Pokemon card packs and merchandise, causing chaos at retailers and even sparking violent confrontations that have ended in arrests.

The hype for GTA 6 is at an all-time high, so we can’t say that these shirts getting resold online is a huge surprise. The city of Miami is even working with Rockstar on some special advertising for the game, having recently erected a massive, $1 million 'Welcome to Vice City' sign after entering talks with officials for a possible GTA 6-themed takeover of the entire area.

items.title: After Asking Very Nicely For a Skin, Madison Beer Joins Fortnite Tomorrow
items.description: Madison Beer is the latest music icon to join the world of Fortnite, after previously issuing a public call to Epic Games for her to become a skin.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Madison Beer is the latest music icon to join the world of Fortnite, after previously issuing a public call to Epic Games for her to become a skin.

The Selfish and Make You Mine singer has long been a fan of Epic Games' battle royale, and has helped promote some of its LEGO-focused modes. Now, Beer is pulling up her socks to join the core Fortnite experience, following her callout to be included — made during an episode of the Hot Ones podcast earlier this year.

Beer follows in the footsteps of other pop icons such as Sabrina Carpenter, Ariana Grande, and Olivia Rodrigo, as well as a swathe of other musical artists including Billie Eilish, Lady Gaga, Eminem and Snoop Dogg, all of whom have multiple in-game skins.

This latest addition will see Beer gain two skins, one of which is themed after her 2025 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show appearance, plus a pickaxe, backblings, emotes, a gun skin, microphone instrument, a loading screen and three more in-game tracks: "yes, baby," "bittersweet," and "complexity."

"I would say this is definitely up there with being nominated for a Grammy and playing Madison Square Garden," Beer said in a statement today. "There's things in my life that I am just obsessed with, and that I would die for, and Fortnite is one of them."

Madison Beer lands in the Fortnite shop tomorrow, and will be streaming the game via Twitch on Friday to celebrate her collaboration finally happening. Who will join Fortnite next?

items.title: Scrapped GTA 5 Story DLC Might Have Taken the Series Overseas for the First Time in 15 Years
items.description: Grand Theft Auto 5's story DLC was seemingly going to take players to Paris, if leaked footage is anything to go by.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 5's story DLC was seemingly going to take players to Paris, if leaked footage is anything to go by.

Last week, a slew of files and assets from GTA 5 surfaced online. This leak showed off variety of cut content, prompting Rockstar to take action and issue takedowns to creators who were showing it in their videos. One of the most interesting parts of this leak has been seeing all of the scrapped DLC, which includes a Liberty City map expansion.

Fans have also uncovered new information about the game's fabled story DLC, which was formally announced by Rockstar in 2013 with a 2014 release window in mind. Unfortunately, none of it ever saw the light of day, as Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA Online became higher priorities. One of the DLCs would've followed Trevor assuming the role of a secret agent, tackling dirty jobs for the government and assassinating powerful foes. Much of this was already known, but what fans likely weren't aware that this DLC was also seemingly going to take players to Paris.

In the leaked files, players were able to look at some of the unfinished levels made for this DLC, and one of them includes some kind of luxury apartment that overlooks Paris. The Eiffel Tower can be seen outside of a balcony, though it's just a flat image rather than an explorable 3D environment. It's entirely possible that this apartment would've been the extent of the overseas adventure, potentially being used for a cutscene or maybe some kind of assassination mission.

The only other time Grand Theft Auto has taken players overseas was in GTA: London 1969, which was an expansion for the original game released in 1999. Some fans have hoped to see the series go abroad, but the franchise's former writer and creative director, Dan Houser, suggested that the series wouldn't work as well outside of America.

"I think for a full GTA game, we always decided there was so much Americana inherent in the IP, it would be really hard to make it work in London or anywhere else," said Houser in 2025. "You know, you needed guns, you needed these larger-than-life characters. It just felt like the game was so much about America, possibly from an outsider's perspective. But that was so much about what the thing was that it wouldn't really have worked in the same way elsewhere.”

Trevor actor Steven Ogg has spoken loosely about the scrapped GTA 5 story DLC in the past. He shot some scenes for it, but Rockstar never followed up on the project, and that was the end of it. A former developer estimated that the DLC was about halfway finished when the plug was pulled and was sour about its cancellation.

“It was really really good," said ex-Rockstar Senior Camera Artist Joe Robino. "But when GTA Online came out, it was so much of a cash cow and people were loving it so much that it was hard to make an argument that a standalone DLC would outcompete that. I think looking back now you could probably do both. But that was a business decision they made. I was a little upset about that. That actually was a lot of the reason for me being a little sour at that time. Because I was like yo, WTF guys? This s**t’s awesome. Let’s keep going. Let’s finish this s**t.”

With GTA 6 on the horizon, it seems unlikely we'll ever see this DLC revived, but some of it was salvaged into GTA Online updates like The Doomsday Heist.

items.title: LEGO One Piece Exclusive Character Posters Revealed
items.description: IGN can exclusively reveal six new character posters from the upcoming two-part LEGO One Piece special, streaming on Netflix on September 29.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
IGN can exclusively reveal six new character posters from the upcoming two-part LEGO One Piece special, streaming on Netflix on September 29. The posters can be seen by scrolling through the gallery below.

The two-part special will revolve around the tall tales Usopp tells Chopper about the Straw Hat Pirates’ adventures across the East Blue and into the Grand Line.

“Set sail with Luffy, Nami, Zoro, Usopp, Sanji, and Chopper as they come together and form the Straw Hat Pirates! In this two-part animated LEGO special, join the crew as they make their way into a treacherous stretch of ocean known as the Grand Line, in search of the One Piece and their dreams,” according to the official synopsis.

“Along the way, they’ll fight off a crazed pirate clown, marines, fishmen, and a criminal syndicate — all while exploring islands full of unknown danger and fun! Oh, and did we mention, the crew’s most reliably unreliable narrator is the teller of this tale? That’s right, Usopp brings his propulsive storytelling and liberal use of “dramatic license” along for the ride.”

The special’s voice cast includes Iñaki Godoy as Monkey D. Luffy, Mackenyu as Zoro, Emily Rudd as Nami, Jacob Romero as Usopp, and Mikaela Hoover as Chopper.

After the LEGO One Piece special, fans expect to see Season 3 of the live-action series – One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta – on Netflix in 2027.

Meanwhile, be sure to read IGN’s One Piece Season 2 review.

items.title: Bethesda Boss Issues Memo to Staff After Xbox Moves Obsidian Into the Fallout Company
items.description: The boss of Bethesda has issued a memo to staff reassuring them that Obsidian Entertainment remains “distinct” despite being absorbed into the company as part of this week’s seismic Xbox studios reorganisation.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The boss of Bethesda has issued a memo to staff reassuring them that Obsidian Entertainment remains “distinct” despite being absorbed into the company as part of this week’s seismic Xbox studios reorganisation.

This week, Microsoft announced hundreds more layoffs as it gutted Halo Studios and handed the next mainline Halo game, Sea of Thieves developer Rare, and Age of Empires developer World's Edge to Activision. Meanwhile, Obsidian, the Microsoft-owned studio behind the likes of Grounded, The Outer Worlds, and Avowed, was made a part of Bethesda.

Obsidian, perhaps most famous for developing the much-loved Fallout: New Vegas, was confirmed to be working on a Fallout game in the wake of new Xbox boss Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business, which has seen nearly 2,000 staff cut in a bid for improved financial performance. More staff are set to lose their jobs over the course of the rest of the current financial year.

Bringing Obsidian into the Bethesda fold makes sense given it’s working on Fallout, but some had worried the move signalled an eventual relegation to Fallout support studio status. But in a memo to staff viewed by IGN, Bethesda boss Jill Braff insisted Obsidian would retain its leadership and identity, while confirming Bethesda Game Studios would “continue to lead the Fallout franchise.”

Here’s the memo in full:

Hi everyone,

Following the note from Matt, I wanted to share more on today’s news and what it means for our collective teams.

I’ve had the opportunity to get to know Feargus Urquhart and his team over the past six years, and I have great respect for what they’ve built. Obsidian has extraordinary creative talent, deep expertise, and a long history of creating memorable games and experiences. I’m looking forward to working more closely with them.

Today’s announcement is primarily a change in reporting structure. The creative identity and strengths that make Obsidian distinct will remain at the core of their studio and work.

Feargus and the Obsidian leadership team will continue to lead Obsidian, with the studio reporting to me. Bethesda Game Studios will continue to lead the Fallout franchise. Together, the teams will build on their longstanding relationship and the early work already underway on a new Fallout project, with more to share in the months ahead. This structure supports the franchise-led model we’ve been strengthening while keeping accountability for both the studio and the franchise clear.

I also recognize that employees across our studios, publishing, and business teams will have questions about what this means for our current priorities, roadmap, and responsibilities. To be clear, we’re not resetting our roadmap or asking teams to change what they’re focused on. We’ll take the time to understand how teams can best support one another, and where closer partnership can benefit our players and fans. We’ll continue communicating as we progress.

I’m looking forward to spending more time with the Obsidian team and building on the strong foundation already in place across our organizations.

Welcome Feargus and team – more soon!

Jill

There is of course a huge amount going on at Bethesda right now, with The Elder Scrolls 6 the focus. Fallout 5 is in pre-production. BGS has also confirmed Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas remasters are in the works. No release windows are known for any of these games, nor Obsidian’s Fallout game.

Meanwhile, BGS has said Starfield "continues," although Bethesda stopped short of confirming a sequel is in the works.

The Xbox “reset” has left Xbox Game Studios a shadow of its former self, with a number of previously owned studios either independent, moved into Activision or Bethesda, or set for closure. Will Gears of War studio The Coalition, which suffered layoffs this week, Clockwork Revolution developer inXile, and Fable and Forza Horizon developer Playground eventually also end up at either Activision or Bethesda?

items.title: Some Fans Seem to Think The Witcher 3 Remastered Looks Worse Than the Original in Official Comparison Clip
items.description: The Witcher 3 fans have reacted to an official comparison clip featuring a snippet of side-by-side gameplay from the original game and the upcoming remaster, with some saying the new version actually looks worse.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The Witcher 3 fans have reacted to an official comparison clip featuring a snippet of side-by-side gameplay from the original game and the upcoming remaster, with some saying the new version actually looks worse.

In the clip, you can see Geralt casting Igni on a group of drowners in the swamp, with a side-by-side comparison with the original game and the remaster. And while the new version of the game has much greater detail on Geralt's armor, along with much more defined water, the reflections seem to be divisive.

Choose your cast - wisely. #TheWitcher3Remastered pic.twitter.com/zcgLSvLvDi

— The Witcher (@thewitcher) September 23, 2026

In the original game, you can see some of the fire reflected in the brackish water underneath the drowners, even if it results in an orange-ish blur. That'd be a pretty low bar to clear with the ray tracing on offer in the remaster, but the clip doesn't show any reflection of the fire at all. The fog is also much different in the remaster. In the original, there are defined clouds of fog floating just above the ground, where the remaster takes a more atmospheric approach to the fog in the distance.

A lot of the differences between the two sides of this clip comes down to the remaster using ray tracing, where the original didn't have it. Fans have had mixed reactions to this clip regardless. X / Twitter user LeafusMaximus said "despite literally adding RT to the game you managed to post a pic with worse water reflections, worse fog effects, worse armor textures in some cases (the glove he keeps back towards the camera for example), the new drowner just look wetter, the old ones actually look scaly/mucky." While desugar_64 simply asked: "Are you sure you didn't swap the footage around?"

Luckily, if you don't like the new visual representation, you should be able to roll back to an earlier version of the build as long as you're playing on PC. I'm not sure if that option will exist on consoles, but if you really don't want your current install of The Witcher 3 to get this change, you can turn off automatic updates. If you are planning on upgrading to the remaster though, you will be able to carry over your save data when the game comes out on September 29.

items.title: 72-Year-Old Pokémon Collector Arrested After Illegally Tracking Woman Who Restocked Local Stores
items.description: A 72-year-old Pokémon card collector has been arrested for illegally tracking a woman who restocked local stores.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
A 72-year-old Pokémon card collector has been arrested for illegally tracking a woman who restocked local stores.

Cleveland resident Kent Kubasta has admitted following the woman's delivery route via an electronic tracker he had secretly placed on her vehicle, in order to see where new card boxes had been dropped off.

According to Fox8, Kubasta entered a plea of no contest to the charge, and declined to comment further when approached by press for an explanation. It is assumed, however, that he was then planning to visit each store and buy up stock as soon as it was placed on sale.

POKÉMON COLLECTOR FOUND GUILTY FOR TRACKING A CARD VENDOR 🚨

A collector used a GPS tracker to follow a woman who stocked Pokémon cards, allowing him to track her route from store to store.

Could’ve just turned notifications on 🤷‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/EpnYUPlg3a

— Reselling News (@resellingnews) September 22, 2026

The tracker was discovered by the driver while dropping cards to a Walmart. A Spytech GPS, the device allowed someone — in this case Kubasta — to follow her movements in real-time via a linked smartphone app.

While word of when and where additional card stock will be available locally is of huge importance to fans struggling to get a hold of the in-demand cards, Kubasta's actions went beyond the usual sharing of intel via social media and online groups, or being tipped off by friendly store owners and delivery drivers. It was also just downright creepy.

Sentencing is yet to take place, but Kubasta could now face up to 180 days in jail and a $1,000 fine.

This month's release of the Pokémon trading card game's 30th Anniversary set has been marred by long lines, "ghost chairs", in-person fights and now frustration from scalpers that rare cards are too easy to find. All of which is bad, except for that last one.

While the 30th Anniversary set has now launched, the next is not far behind. Earlier this week, IGN revealed three new card designs from the upcoming set Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign set, a fresh batch of Mega Evolution-themed cards that is due out on November 6.

items.title: Yet Another Disney+ Price Hike Is Coming — and It's Reportedly Due This Week
items.description: Disney plans to raise the price of Disney+ this week, according to a new report.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Disney plans to raise the price of Disney+ this week, according to a new report.

Bloomberg said Disney+ without ads will go up by $2.50 — or 13% — to $21.49 per month. That’s closer to Netflix’s ad-free subscription, which costs $26.99 a month with 4K resolution and access on multiple devices.

According to the same report, Hulu without advertising is going up by the same amount. The ad-free subscription bundle including both Disney+ and Hulu increases by $2 to $21.99, or just 50 cents more than subscribing to each service individually.

The price rises are set to kick in today, Wednesday 23, for new subscribers, according to Bloomberg. Existing customers must pay the new prices from their next monthly bill. The ad-free Disney+ tier was just $10.99 a month just three years ago in 2023.

The news comes just days after Disney+ altered its user agreement for subscribers in Europe to clarify that ads will be allowed before and after playback on all subscription tiers. Subscribers in the U.S. have currently not received an updated agreement.

Disney+ has seen a number of price rises in recent years, most recently in October 2025. You can see the full line-up of content made available on the streaming service for September 2026 here.

items.title: Sony Patent Would Let You Tap Your Card or Phone on Your PlayStation Controller to Make a Payment
items.description: Sony filed a patent called "video game controller-driven information transfer," and describes a controller with NFC capabilities, which would let you tap your phone or your credit card to your controller to send information to your console.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Both Sony and Microsoft have had a series of patents come out in the last week or so, and one of them would potentially bring NFC payments to the PlayStation 6.

Sony filed a patent called "video game controller-driven information transfer," which describes a controller with NFC capabilities that would let you tap your phone or your credit card to your controller to send information to your console. The most obvious use for this would be for payment, but it would also let you more easily import your PlayStation account to a new console.

Just like with any patent, there's no guarantee that this would result in an actual feature for any device, but if it did, it wouldn't be the first time this type of feature has existed. Pretty much every phone under the sun right now has similar functionality, which lets you tap your card to add it to your wallet, or tap bluetooth headphones to pair them without digging through the settings menu. So, it seems like a no-brainer to bring that functionality in some way to a console.

There are of course some security issues that Sony would have to work out before implementing this, particularly if Sony wants you to import your whole account via this method. Without the right precautions, it'd be easy to grab someone's phone, tap it to your controller and effectively use their account.

Apple gets around this when setting up a new iPhone or iPad by bringing up a cloud that you have to scan with the new device's camera that will then give permission to import the account data. It's unlikely that Sony is going to put a camera in a controller, but a more simple option would be to have your phone display a pin number that you'd have to enter into the console to get past a security check.

What's particularly wild about this patent, though, is some of the rationale behind developing it. In the patent documentation, Sony talks about the traditional methods to input this data, like an on-screen keyboard or a QR code that you scan with your phone. But, then goes on to say "facilitating and coordinating these operations by performing multiple operational steps using multiple devices often causes performance of the video game console to suffer and/or one or more operations of the video game console to fail."

The idea here seems to be that importing all the account data through NFC will be more reliable than the current methods, and could prevent any kind of system failures during setup. NFC communication has become a lot better in recent years, to be sure, but whether it's going to make the system less prone to failure than typing in your data via a keyboard is something that'd I'd need to see to believe.

With all of the patents that have been coming out in the last couple weeks, it sure does seem like the next-generation consoles are actually on the way. Microsoft and Sony have both filed some pretty dystopian patents, but this one seems like it'd be genuinely useful. Either way, though, expect both the PlayStation 6 and Xbox Project Helix to be quite expensive, especially if they're announced amid the ongoing RAM crisis continues.

items.title: Xbox Mythic Achievement Will Be Microsoft's Version of a Platinum Trophy — And It Has an Extravagant Unlock Sound
items.description: Microsoft is expected to imminently launch Xbox Mythic Achievements, its own version of PlayStation's platinum Trophies, and you can now hear how they will sound when unlocked.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Microsoft is expected to imminently launch Xbox Mythic Achievements, its own version of PlayStation's platinum Trophies, and you can now hear how they will sound when unlocked.

Xbox has previously confirmed plans to introduce its own method of tracking your full completion of a game — that is, when you have unlocked all of a title's 1,000 Gamerscore by nabbing every single Achievement.

Now, an update to the Xbox PC app has revealed the sound effect for an Xbox Mythic Achievement being unlocked, which has been discovered buried within the update's files. You can hear its rather majestic audio cue just below, courtesy of Xbox leaker Klobrille.

A new update for the Xbox PC App reveals: Xbox Mythic Achievement; plus symbol and unlock sound.

The Xbox Mythic Achievement is expected to be a 100% Gamerscore game completion reward. pic.twitter.com/STLisa4ubz

— Klobrille (@klobrille) September 22, 2026

The sound is a suitably more grandiose version of the regular achievement unlock ping, which already can be heard in a more dramatic form when a rare achievement (owned by only a small percentage of players) is unlocked instead.

Microsoft's new Xbox Mythic Achievement effect is longer and more majestic still, lasting around 15 seconds as the audio wooshes in, builds, and then reverberates around. It's satisfying stuff, though whether it'll actually encourage you to grind for hours to get that full 1000G is entirely your choice.

Back in the day, Xbox Achievements were the first standardized reward system on a console platform, launching in 2005 back on the Xbox 360. The concept was so popular that Valve introduced Steam achievements in 2007, while Sony added Trophies to the PS3 in 2008.

While games typically share awards lists across platforms (so Xbox Achievements and PlayStation Trophy requirements are typically similar), Sony platforms have long featured the extra Platinum Trophy for most games, unlocked alongside your final regular Trophy. It is a signifier that you have truly mastered everything a game might have to offer, and fans' Platinum Trophy counts have themselves become something to collect and show off.

Microsoft is yet to say when Xbox Mythic Achievements will land across the Xbox ecosystem, but today's leak certainly suggests it won't be long now.

items.title: Sony PlayStation Patent Would Solve System Problems With AI Vibe-Coded Patches
items.description: Anyone who's had a console knows that on a long enough timeline they will have some kind of technical bug that you need to troubleshoot, and Sony is trying to get around that reality with an AI tech support agent.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Anyone who's had a console knows that, on a long-enough timeline, they will have some kind of technical bug that you need to troubleshoot. Sony is trying to get around that reality with an AI tech support agent.

Sony has filed a patent for an AI that would keep an eye on your system, looking for any kind of red flags, and then use an LLM to write up a patch for your system to either preemptively fix the issue or to send a report to engineers at Sony. The problem is, that unless you can turn this feature off, all the data processed on your PlayStation would potentially be visible to this agent. It would likely need total access to successfully monitor a system for any and all hardware and software issues.

It's also possible that the system could make small issues into much larger ones. As Patentlyze found, the patent says "an automated system sending repair instructions to a device in your living room needs careful guardrails so a small hiccup does not become a larger one." After all, the PlayStation 5 (and likely the PlayStation 6) are just specialized computers, and there have been plenty of times that I've broken something by fixing a small problem that I probably could have just ignored (or wasn't a real problem to begin with).

There's also a possibility that, unless the LLM has particularly strong training and guardrails, that it could make a mistake when coding these on-demand patches, and accidentally brick people's PlayStations.

It's not clear when or if this patent will actually materialize into an AI tech support agent for your PlayStation. items.title: Ray Gunn Debut Trailer Confirms Limited Theatrical Release for Brad Bird's Netflix Movie
items.description: Netflix has released the debut trailer for Ray Gunn, the next animated movie from The Incredibles director Brad Bird.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Netflix has released the debut trailer for Ray Gunn, the next animated movie from The Incredibles director Brad Bird.

Ray Gunn, the first Brad Bird-directed movie since 2018’s Incredibles 2, will see a limited theatrical release from December 4, with the movie streaming on Netflix itself from December 18.

Welcome to the future. From the director of The Incredibles and Ratatouille comes RAY GUNN, starring Sam Rockwell, Scarlett Johansson, and Tom Waits.

In select theaters December 4 and on Netflix December 18. pic.twitter.com/4r2rtjCC8v

— Netflix (@netflix) September 23, 2026

Here’s the official blurb:

Academy Award winner Brad Bird, the visionary director of The Incredibles, Ratatouille, and The Iron Giant, brings you a whole new world to investigate…
In Metropia, a gigantic city in an alternate future as seen from 1939, private eye Raymond Gunn (Sam Rockwell) is drawn into a case involving aliens, murder and a multimedia star named Venus Nova (Scarlett Johansson).

"Ray Gunn has been in my mind for over 30 years," Bird said. "The film is a blend of sci-fi and classic detective movies from the '40s...it's Maltese Falcon meets Buck Rogers. I've been a fan of both of those sort of genres, and blending them together seemed fun, and a chance to play with a lot of very cinematic elements, and extreme characters."

items.title: 'I Had 3 More Star Wars to Make' — George Lucas Reveals What He Left Behind When He Retired From Making Movies
items.description: George Lucas planned three more Star Wars movies before he ultimately decided to retire, with Disney taking up the franchise instead.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
George Lucas planned three more Star Wars movies before he ultimately decided to retire, with Disney taking up the franchise instead.

Lucas has, over the years, occasionally discussed having nebulous ideas for his own Star Wars sequel trilogy, though nothing concrete was set in motion before he sold the series to Disney for $4 billion back in 2012. The filmmaker has also made conflicting statements over the past 50 years over whether he ever had ideas for a third trilogy of stories in the first place.

Still, Lucas has now referenced an abandoned desire to complete what has become known as the "Skywalker Saga" — all nine main Star Wars films — though Lucas has said he had to choose between creating those and working on his newly-opened museum.

"When I did this, I decided to retire from making movies," Lucas said of creating The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, in conversation with CBS. "Which was a big deal because I had three more Star Wars to make.

"But I realized that I was running out of time," he continued, "and I did want to make this museum, and I'd spent a lot of time developing digital technology for the movie business. You know, all art depends on technology."

Lucas' early plans for the Star Wars sequel trilogy changed dramatically over time, with ideas that it would feature a sister for Luke Skywalker and an ultimate showdown with Emperor Palpatine reworked into Return of the Jedi. By the 1980s, Lucas realized the sheer scale of the story, and elected to make just the main trilogy.

Of course, Lucas did eventually go on to write and direct the prequel trilogy, to greater and lesser success, but this experience reportedly soured him against continuing the Star Wars saga further. By the time of the 1990s, after nine years of production on the Star Wars prequels, Lucas sounded particularly unenthused at the prospect of another decade making movies.

"Basically what I said as a joke was, 'Maybe when Harrison and Carrie are in their 70s, we'll come back and do another version,'" Ford told Starlog magazine in 2002. "The thing I didn't realize then, and that I do realize now very clearly, is that not only would they be in their 70s, but I would be in my 70s too."

While Star Wars' third trilogy was eventually made by Disney, again to greater and lesser success, the Mickey Mouse company still incorporated several ideas that Lucas himself has said he originated. These included plans for its story to be set around 30 years after Return of the Jedi, with an older Mark Hamill, Harrison Ford, and Carrie Fisher all returning. Lucas also had plans for Luke's role to be "much more ethereal," potentially on another plane of existence entirely, which doesn't sound too dissimilar to where Skywalker ends up.

As part of the same interview, Lucas also defended his constant tinkering with the original Star Wars trilogy, which has undergone at least four rounds of changes since its release.

items.title: Avengers: Endgame Encore Leaks Reveal New Ending and Additional Scenes That Connect to Avengers: Doomsday, Including Several Unannounced Cast Members
items.description: Four new scenes included in Avengers: Endgame Encore have leaked online, including a tweaked ending to the 2019 Marvel blockbuster.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Four new scenes included in Avengers: Endgame Encore have leaked online, including a tweaked ending to the 2019 Marvel blockbuster.

These additional extras have been designed to link Endgame directly to the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, and also to encourage theatregoers to rewatch the last Avengers film all over again to swell Marvel's coffers — er, I mean, to prep themselves for what's next.

Warning! Spoilers for Avengers: Endgame Encore follow:

Inevitably, footage has emerged from early screenings of Avengers: Endgame Encore showing the new scenes in full, which Marvel is now scrambling to scrub from social media. However, IGN has reviewed numerous copies of the scenes today before they were deleted from X/Twitter via copyright claim — thereby confirming their legitimacy.

Most notably, the scenes include multiple characters whose appearance in Doomsday had not previously been revealed. Since these extra moments are believed to have been filmed during Doomsday's production, it's now likely we'll be seeing more of these characters in December, when Doomsday itself arrives.

Steve's Dance Is Interrupted

The first extra scene acts as a new ending to Endgame, and merges directly with the pre-existing finale that fans already know and love: Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter reunited, sharing a dance, and settling down to a quiet life together.

Except the couple's quiet moment together is now interrupted by a knock at their door. Cautiously, Peggy opens it to reveal Loki, who greets the couple, as Steve looks surprised.

A few things here are immediately obvious — this is the version of Loki who has joined the TVA (the Time Variance Authority, essentially Marvel's multiverse police) but before he ends up becoming the all-powerful replacement of Kang. All of this fits with long-held leaked information that suggests Loki moves Steve and Peggy (and their son) to another branch of the multiverse for their own protection, several years before the main events of Doomsday take place.

Hulk Is Collected

During Endgame Encore's credits, the first all-new scene features Mark Ruffalo as Bruce Banner (and briefly, off-screen, the Hulk). This appears to be our first confirmation that the character will indeed appear in Avengers: Doomsday, after last being seen in bad shape at the end of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

Indeed, this scene picks up a little while after Hulk is taken away, seemingly out of action following a destructive stint as his green alter ego. Now secluded in an old military bunker two miles underground, Banner records a video where he begins to discuss his work creating a new stabilizing serum. And, of course, he states that no one can get into the bunker to disturb.

Unfortunately, his video (and his work on that serum) are interrupted by the arrival of Doctor Doom into the bunker to disturb him. While kept offscreen, we hear Robert Downey Jr'.s voice say that he's come to "collect" Banner, as the scientist seemingly morphs into the Hulk once more. Has Doom enslaved Hulk, or sought to absorb his power somehow? We'll have to wait and see.

The TVA Realizes the Multiverse Is Collapsing

The next all-new scene is set within the TVA, presumably in the time after Loki has ascended to godhood. His former colleagues Mobius (Owen Wilson), Casey (Eugene Cordero) and Ouroboros (Ke Huy Quan) all panic as they spot a pair of Earths from different universes about to collide, and which begin to attack each other. One of these Earths is Universe-1005, the Fox X-Men universe, which ties into long-held leaks that the mutant team has been surviving incursions by wiping out other universes first. (I sure hope they don't have to destroy a universe with any other beloved Marvel character in it!)

Things quickly get worse, however, as the TVA team quickly realizes that the entire multiverse is collapsing, with thousands of universes now at risk of being annihilated through incursions.

While some involvement of the TVA in Doomsday seemed likely, none of these characters have previously been confirmed to return for the film. Indeed, none have been seen since the finale of Loki, which wrapped up in 2023. Tara Strong's animated Miss Minutes also features here, too.

Doctor Doom Makes an Iron Man Reference

At the end of Endgame Encore's credits, one final snippet sees Doctor Doom hammering his metal mask into shape. This is a clear and obvious nod to Iron Man (also played by Robert Downey Jr.!) who created his first mask in the same way, and a reference to the original ending of Endgame, which featured the same hammer sounds heard here (which come from the first 2008 Iron Man film).

Maybe the Russos always knew this post-credits tease would eventually be changed to feature Doctor Doom! Or, maybe, this is just a really clever callback.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, and I'm genuinely more excited to see it after watching all of these. Are you headed to Avengers: Endgame Encore to catch them on the big screen?

items.title: ‘Vice City’ Trademark Abandoned by WWE ahead of GTA 6 launch
items.description: With GTA 6 imminent, it appears that WWE was trying to trademark the term ‘Vice City,’ before abandoning plans to do so.
items.author: Simon Cardy
items.content:
It appears that WWE was trying to trademark the term ‘Vice City,’ before abandoning plans to do so.

According to a trademark filing, the initial application was made on August 8, before being deemed “dead’ just over a month later, on September 21.

No, it doesn’t appear that WWE was attempting to make its own Grand Theft Auto game, but it was more than likely an attempt to theme something around Lola Vice, a WWE wrestler who has recently been promoted to the main roster. It’s not just her in-ring name that suggests this was the case either, but also the fact that she is from Miami, Florida, the real-life location GTA’s Vice City is based on.

While we don’t know the reasons as to why the trademark was abandoned by WWE, it’s fair to speculate that Rockstar Games wouldn’t have taken kindly to someone else trying to claim ownership over a name it has used for over two decades. Vice City is, of course, the setting of the PS2 classic GTA Vice City and the upcoming GTA 6. You’d have to imagine Triple H and co. knew this, but still tried their arm anyway.

The extent to which Rockstar is reminding people of this can be seen in real-life Miami now, with nearly $1 million spent on ‘Welcome to Vice City’ signage.

Incidentally, backyard wrestling looks set to be one of the many, many activities available for Jason and Lucia to engage with in GTA 6, with even a nod to John Cena’s Attitude Adjustment finisher spotted in the recent extended look at the game. You can check out that and 99 details we spotted in our first look at gameplay here.

GTA 6 is seemingly set to take over the world when it launches on November 19, and the world of sports and entertainment won’t be unaffected by it. So much so that NBA star Steven Adams has claimed that he expects the launch of Rockstar’s latest to lead to a “league-wide” drop in performance for basketball players and coaches.

It’s already been a busy week for the GTA and Red Dead Redemption studio, as we imagine every week will be from now until the release of GTA 6. The developer has taken down footage of scrapped GTA 5 DLC and an early version of a leaked GTA 6 map, and has outlined its new modding policy, as dreams of monetized GTA 6 RP servers appear to have been dashed.

items.title: Frodo's Back! Set Photos From The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum Offer Behind-the-Scenes Look at Prequel Movie
items.description: Warner Bros. has released set photos from The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum to celebrate Hobbit Day, revealing a first look at Frodo and the Shire.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Warner Bros. has released set photos from The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum to celebrate Hobbit Day, revealing a first look at Frodo and the Shire.

The prequel movie, currently filming in New Zealand with a release date of December 17, 2027, sees Elijah Wood reprise his iconic role as Frodo Baggins. This peek at the character, released on Warner Bros.' TikTok page, doesn’t tell us much other than Frodo looks a lot like Frodo should. Unfortunately, as we’re only seeing Frodo’s back, we can’t see Wood’s face in character. I suspect that’s because the de-aging technology will be applied later on, so showing the character in full now wouldn’t accurately represent what fans will see in theaters.

But we do see plenty of Hobbits in the shire, as well as director and Gollum actor Andy Serkis working a camera. It’s all very nostalgic and pretty.

Hobbit day Hunt For Gollum photos
by u/DryScholar8371 in lotr

The Hunt for Gollum will reunite Serkis with his fellow Lord of the Rings co-stars Ian McKellen as Gandalf and the aforementioned Wood as Frodo, with Lee Pace reprising his role as elven king Thranduil from The Hobbit film trilogy. New additions to the cast include Fifty Shades of Grey actor Jamie Dornan, who takes over from Viggo Mortensen as Aragorn, and The Super Mario Bros. Movie actress Anya Taylor-Joy, who plays a new "lethal elf" named Seren.

Serkis hit the headlines in July when he discussed The Hunt for Gollum's use of AI to digitally de-age some of The Lord of the Rings' aging stars, who need to look younger than they did 25 years ago in Fellowship of the Ring. "There’s a little bit of de-aging for some of the characters and machine learning is part of the process," Serkis said.

The movie revolves around various characters tracking down Gollum in order to discover the location of the One Ring. This time period is briefly shown during Fellowship's prologue, and covered briefly in Tolkien's original writings.

"I'm leaving him to it," The Lord of the Rings director Peter Jackson said previously of Serkis taking the helm. "I'm there to help if I can help, if I can be of assistance at certain times, I'm there. But I'm giving him as much freedom as I can, because giving Andy freedom to make that movie will result in the best possible film."

Image credit: Warner Bros.

items.title: Star Wars Zero Company Estimated to Have Sold 1 Million, With Nearly 70% on Steam
items.description: Star Wars Zero Company is estimated to have sold 1 million copies, with the majority of those sales coming from Steam.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Star Wars Zero Company is estimated to have sold 1 million copies, with the majority of those sales coming from Steam.

Alinea Analytics' Rhys Elliott took to social media to discuss the performance of Bit Reactor’s Star Wars strategy game, which was developed by former developers of XCOM at Firaxis.

69.9% of those 1 million sales came from Steam, with 19.9% on PlayStation, and 10.2% on Xbox / Xbox PC. Clearly, Steam is where it’s at for Zero Company, which Elliott estimates has generated around $50 million since last month’s launch.

This performance, Elliott said, is “respectable for this genre and during such a crowded period (even with the Star Wars brand attached).”

But does it meet publisher EA’s expectations? The company has yet to issue official sales figures for Zero Company or comment on its commercial performance. Now EA has gone private, it is under no obligation to share revenue figures with the market, so it’s unlikely we’ll find out.

What we do know is that Bit Reactor furloughed "many of its workers" before Zero Company even came out as it reportedly had "run out of most of its money just ahead of the launch of its first game." Bit Reactor told Game File it was a "difficult decision" made "before it was clear how the launch would go," insisting it was not influenced by EA or Star Wars rights holder Disney. Game File reported that 80% of Bit Reactor’s staff were furloughed, leaving a skeleton crew to address any post-launch bugs for Zero Company.

“It's SO GOOD, but it's niche,” Elliott added. “One thing limiting Zero Company’s sales, as with many Star Wars games, is that it’s only really popular in the West. Of Zero Company’s players, 90% are in North America or Europe, with under 5% in Asia.

items.title: George Lucas Says His Changes to The Original Star Wars Trilogy Were Justified as Movies Always Get 'Yanked Out of Your Hands' For Release
items.description: Star Wars creator George Lucas has defended his frequent tweaks to the series' original movies, while acknowledging "a lot of people got upset" about the changes.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Star Wars creator George Lucas has defended his frequent tweaks to the series' original movies, while acknowledging that "a lot of people got upset" about the changes.

Lucas' numerous updates to the classic Star Wars trilogy have become a legendary source of debate for fans, with each of Lucas' many, many subsequent alterations sparking discussion on whether they were advisable or necessary.

The trilogy's 1997 Special Edition release, which made major alterations and added an array of new CGI effects, was mostly well-received (with one notable exception we'll get to below). But Lucas has continued to tinker with the movies in the years since. Further changes were made to the movies for their DVD release in 2004, and again for their Blu-ray launch in 2011. More minor adjustments were even made for their Disney+ launch in 2019, over 40 years on from their original debut.

Some of these changes are unlikely to register to casual viewers, such as Obi-Wan Kenobi's shout to scare off the Tusken Raiders on Tatooine (which was changed for the 2004 DVD release, and then again for the 2011 Blu-ray). Others are more technical in nature, fixing color mistakes or improving the appearance of matte backgrounds.

But other edits have sparked significant criticism, such as the changes made to link the original movies with Lucas' prequel trilogy (such as the digital removal of Anakin Skywalker's eyebrows for Return of the Jedi's launch on DVD, or the addition of Hayden Christensen as Anakin's Force ghost).

And then there's the infamous 'who shot first?' debate in A New Hope's scene with Han Solo and the bounty hunter Greedo. The identity of who shot first (and the resulting implications this had for Han's personality) was reversed in the 1997 Special Edition, shortened for the 2004 DVD, shortened further for the 2011 Blu-ray, and even tweaked with new visual effects in a 2019.

Reflecting on the changes now in an interview with CBS, Lucas characterized his edits as him finally getting a chance to complete his stories, after initially having to meet production deadlines.

"Most movies aren't finished, they're simply yanked out of your hands and put in the theaters," Lucas said. "So you're always saying 'oh, I wish I could have just finished that one piece of thing.' But it's not that way. You have a deadline, you've got to make the deadline.

"But then I went back, after Star Wars, and redid all the movies, in terms of finishing them. So that they're actually finished. And of course, a lot of people got upset about that, because they said 'you're not allowed to do that.' I said 'fans are doing that. They're making alternate versions and all kinds of stuff.'"

Of course, it is Lucas' right to revisit his work however he pleases — and it is also the right of Star Wars fans to have their say in response. But Lucas concluded by mentioning how vociferous the debate around Star Wars has now become. The creator has previously suggested that the negative fan reaction to his changes (and his prequel movies) was a factor in his ultimate decision to sell the franchise to Disney.

"It's hard to explain to the studios that if you listen to the people who are unhappy, it's not going to turn out well," Lucas noted. "It's going to be sad. Because they're not people who know how to make movies."

For those keen to see Star Wars in all its 1977 glory, the original movie will return to theaters (without all of Lucas' subsequent changes) for a limited release in February 2027, in honor of the film's 50th anniversary.

Image credit: Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Lucas Museum of Narrative Art.
